summary: Yaping Dou works in religious and Buddhist studies. Dou completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xue Yu (attested 2010).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Komarovski studied at Tibetan monastic institutes under teachers including Lobsang Gyatso, and at the University of Virginia. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University and a post at University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011-2015).

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1962-1967). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1978, ~1996).

Yasuaki Nara (1929-2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Calcutta under Kogen Mizuno and Hajime Nakamura. He served at Komazawa University from 1960 and the Sōtō Zen Center in 2000.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed a PhD at UC Berkeley (~1978-1983). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology, National Institutes for the Humanities, and Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971-1975) and served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~2018).

Yasuhiro Okazaki is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. Okazaki has held posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied briefly at Tübingen University Library under George Baumann and held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996-2012).

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He is attested in 2026 as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Yasuhiro Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies. He conducted doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003-2004) and held a research post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929-2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950-1954). He served as an associate professor at Shuchiin University (1966-2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1976-2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1968-1973). He spent his main academic career at Kyoto University (1973-2004), becoming a professor and professor emeritus, alongside posts at Kindai University and Minpaku.

Yasuko Kojima specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. Kojima is attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasumasa Sekine is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His academic posts include positions at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima (1939-1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Göttingen, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1987-1999) and head of the JAIBS.
Yasunori Mibu specializes in Buddhist studies. Mibu earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Yasuo Deguchi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1987-1991). He served at Nagoya Institute of Technology, founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy, and became a professor and dean at Kyoto University.

Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who has served as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held a technical post at Nara National Museum (~1995-2004) and took up a position at Kyoto University in ~2004.

Yasuo Matsunami (1946-2010) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano, served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995-2006), and was advisor to the Sravakabhumi Study Group until 2010.
